text:
sara_sales: FYI customer POC failing when routing to our Private box over their site-to-site IPsec tunnel. They see TLS handshake errors + 502s. Need swarming help, customer blocker for renewal call tomorrow.
sara_sales: top symptoms: intermittent 502, TLS handshake_failure in client logs, and some 429s from our edge when retries happen. They say firewall team sees fragmented packets.
kevin_se: can you paste the TLS client log and a tcpdump? Also which deployment — Private VPC or on-prem package?
sara_sales: it's our Private on-prem package (customer-managed IPsec VPN to our co-lo). NAT at the edge on their side. attaching snippets below.
sara_sales: ```
TLS error: TLSv1.3 alert handshake_failure
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
curl: (56) Received HTTP/2 stream 0 was not closed cleanly: INTERNAL_ERROR (err 2)
X-Redwood-Proxy: upstream 502
```
kevin_se: ok two likely causes: (1) cert chain/trust path broken due to MTU causing fragmentation of the server cert during handshake, (2) SNI/Host header mismatch because NAT or route rewrite. Can you run these checks:
kevin_se: ```
# from their client/network
openssl s_client -connect 10.12.5.7:443 -servername api.customer-poc.redwood.example -showcerts
# and from our edge path
tcpdump -nni any 'tcp port 443' -c 200 -w /tmp/poc_tls.pcap
```
ian_neteng: also have them check for DF/MSS issues on the IPsec tunnel. MFU/MTU clamping on tunnel endpoints is common. If MSS is too high, the TLS certificate (which can be large) might be fragmented and dropped by middleboxes. Quick mitigation: clamp MSS on their firewall / set tcp-mss on the tunnel.
ian_neteng: iptables rule they can apply (temporary) -> `iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` or set peering MTU to 1400.
alice_support: can you also include the full Host header/curl command for reproducing? sometimes our router needs Host mapping for private endpoints.
sara_sales: reproducer we gave them: `curl -v --resolve api.customer-poc.redwood.example:443:10.12.5.7 https://api.customer-poc.redwood.example/health` -> returns 502. Verbose TLS shows handshake_failure above.
kevin_se: run with openssl s_client output — if you see server sends CertificateMessage split across TCP segments, suspect middlebox. You can also try `openssl s_client -tls1_2` to see fallback behavior.
marta_security: quick security Q from their vendor questionnaire: where are TLS private keys stored for Private on-prem? Customer wants KMS/HSM details before we change config.
sara_sales: we told them keys are customer-managed in their HSM, server cert is from their CA hosted in their KMS. We do not hold customer private keys for Private on-prem.
pricing_bot: note: customer asked about cost if we move them to a dedicated reserved pool for this POC spike. Estimate sent?
sara_sales: not yet — can we get a ballpark for a 4-week dedicated GPU pod + private egress? we need a quick quote to unblock procurement.
kevin_se: separate from network fix — I'll ping infra for an emergency quote. For the POC blocker, can you run these two tests and paste the openssl output?
sara_sales: pasted openssl output: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = Example Root CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
139628439347808:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:SSL alert number 46
```
ian_neteng: that verify error can be red herring if they don't have the intermediate locally. But the alert suggests remote closed connection. Did they try lowering MTU?
sara_sales: they applied the iptables MSS clamp and re-ran curl -> now they get 200 OK from /health. customer confirmed TLS handshakes succeed.
sara_sales: 
customer: "After lowering MSS on the tunnel our app can complete TLS handshake and we see no 502s. Thanks."
kevin_se: great — root cause: IPsec tunnel MTU/MSS causing TLS cert fragmentation and handshake aborts at a middlebox (their firewall). Permanent fix: set tunnel MTU to 1400 or apply MSS clamping on the customer edge.
ian_neteng: added note: also verify their NAT device preserves SNI (don't rewrite TLS ClientHello). If they ever rotate to a PrivateLink style endpoint, make sure SNI mapping is configured.
marta_security: tagging that in the security questionnaire: network-level mitigations required, call out that customer-managed edge must allow full TLS handshake & not terminate TLS.
sara_sales: closing loop — blocking network issue resolved. still need quick pricing quote for dedicated 4-week pod, and need legal to confirm private key statement in questionnaire.
pricing_bot: created quote request Q-7891 and assigned to finance for same-day response.
alice_support: opened internal ticket: PRIVATE-SUPPORT-1234 and assigned kevin + ian. ops-bot: <ticket link>
kevin_se: will follow up with customer tomorrow on final validation and capture a postmortem we can reuse in future POCs. :thumbsup:
